clue.text: Fights to show positive things following reform

indicators.note: the positive things come after the reform, so CATIONS goes second

parts.note: to reform something is to alter it
cations are positively charged ions

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a shake-up will be proved worthwhile by the good things that come after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Positive things' reads as benefits, but here it is chemistry: a cation is a positively charged ion.
explanation.definitionFit: Altercations are noisy quarrels or disputes, a milder sense of fights.

clue.text: Hoped despair might be resolved

indicators.note: the letters of despair could be broken down and settled into a new order

explanation.surface: Hopelessness might yet be cleared up, which is itself a kind of hoping.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim or long for something, so aspired is a synonym of hoped in the past tense.

clue.text: Ultimately pot white, perhaps, being in tangle

indicators.note: the final letter of the word pot is taken

parts.note: last letter of pot
white is one kind of wine, so the example stands for the class

explanation.surface: A snooker player finally pots the white ball and ends up in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot white' looks like snooker, where the white is the cue ball; here white is a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to twist or wind strands together, which is to tangle or entwine them.

clue.text: Shop around one to get alcoholic drink, in principle

indicators.note: rat on is placed around the one, enclosing it

parts.note: to shop someone is to rat on them, to inform on them
I is the Roman numeral one
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: In principle, a shopper goes around the bar to get one alcoholic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' looks like a store or buying; it is the British slang verb meaning to inform on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or principle behind a course of action.

clue.text: Regret getting naked to get the last word

indicators.note: stripping off the outer covering means losing the outside letters of the word

parts.note: to lament is to regret or mourn

explanation.surface: Someone regrets stripping off, which proves to be the end of the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the very end of a prayer or hymn, so it is literally the closing word.

clue.text: Back home at 6 am? Sit in the sunlight

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as a phrase: ..., what you are if you only get home at dawn
second meaning: to expose to the sun's rays

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles home at dawn, then goes to sit out in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic reading: split the answer as IN SO LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolate is a rare verb for exposing something to sunlight, from Latin sol, the sun.

clue.text: Irishman upset, clenching tense buttocks

indicators.note: the reversed name grips the letter inside it
in a down clue, upset means the name is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An upset Irishman tightens his buttocks in tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Nates is the anatomical Latin plural for the buttocks.

clue.text: When making comeback, Five also rope in old European

indicators.note: coming back means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
a guy is a rope that steadies a tent or mast

explanation.surface: A sports team called the Five stage a comeback, roping in a veteran European player.
explanation.walkthrough: Five, also and rope give V ALSO GUY; reading that string backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yugoslavia broke up in the 1990s, so a Yugoslav is a citizen of a European country that no longer exists.

clue.text: Part of Chevrolet, for example, belonging to fleeing criminal

indicators.note: the possessive word runs away, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: an offender is a criminal
of means belonging to, as in the house of my father

explanation.surface: A car part, such as one off a Chevrolet, turns out to belong to a criminal on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: Chevrolet is an American car maker, so the American word is apt: a fender is what the British call a car's wing.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a fender is the wing panel over a car's wheel, so it is a component of a Chevy.

clue.text: Artist wound hair

parts.note: a wound is a hurt, a source of pain
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: An artist has twisted her hair up, or an artist is pained about her hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like the past tense of wind, as in hair wound into a bun; it is the noun for an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintress is an old feminine form of painter, a woman who paints pictures.

clue.text: Caught breaking legitimate ceasefire

indicators.note: the abbreviation breaks into the word, sitting inside it

parts.note: true in the sense of genuine, rightful
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught violating a lawful ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreed pause in fighting, the same thing as a ceasefire.

clue.text: Polygynous South African maybe swipes to the left, then all right

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the left means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: swipes is old British slang for weak or poor beer
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A dating-app user with several partners, maybe South African, swipes left and then says everything is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a dating app, where swiping left rejects someone; here swipes means beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The reebok, or rhebok, is a South African antelope; males keep several females, hence polygynous.

clue.text: Bother over papers showing fossil

parts.note: blast is an exclamation of annoyance, like bother
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone curses as the newspapers report a fossil find.
explanation.definitionFit: A blastoid is an extinct echinoderm known only from fossil remains of the Palaeozoic era.

clue.text: Shame of semi-nude chap taking ecstasy

indicators.note: half of the word nude is kept, here its second half

parts.note: the back half of nude

indicators.note: the man takes the drug in, holding it inside

parts.note: a chap is a man
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A half-dressed man high on drugs disgraces himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to humiliate or degrade them, which is to shame them.

clue.text: Couple on the up retreat to get physical

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: to mate is to couple, to pair

indicators.note: going up a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a lair is a den, a place to retreat to

explanation.surface: A pair on the rise go off to a getaway to get fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Material can mean bodily or physical rather than spiritual, as in the material world.

clue.text: Sister admits interest in pedant

indicators.note: the abbreviation lets the other word in, so it sits inside

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for sister, as for a nun
to tickle someone's fancy is to interest them

explanation.surface: A nun confesses she is fascinated by a fussy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on rules being followed to the letter, just as a pedant fusses over details.

clue.text: Push to predict lucky escape

parts.note: you push a door or lid to close it
to call an outcome, such as a coin toss, is to predict it

explanation.surface: A pushy instruction to forecast a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call is a near miss, a situation in which disaster was only narrowly avoided.

clue.text: Flying birdmen describing love for seaside resort

indicators.note: to describe is to draw round, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
the letters of birdmen are sent up in the air and land in a fresh order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Hang-gliding stuntmen circle above a holiday beach while declaring their love for it.
explanation.walkthrough: BENIDRM, the anagram of birdmen, goes around O. Benidorm is a Spanish Costa Blanca resort famous for British package holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Benidorm is a high-rise beach holiday town on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: That place that India claims is owing money

indicators.note: India takes the place in, holding it within itself

parts.note: IND is the international code for India
there means that place

explanation.surface: A disputed region claimed by India is said to be in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the red means having an overdrawn account, since debts were once entered in red ink.

clue.text: Challenge naughty child with adapted gun

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: the gun is modified, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tearaway child challenges someone with a modified weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to dispute or question its truth, so it means to challenge it.

clue.text: Perhaps crow or rook overwhelmed by virus

indicators.note: the letter is swamped, sitting inside the virus

parts.note: Covid is the coronavirus disease
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird, a crow or rook, falls victim to a virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like another bird alongside crow; it is the chess piece, R in notation.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow belongs to the family Corvidae, so a crow is an example of a corvid.

clue.text: Extremely dirty and unpleasant house

indicators.note: only the extremes of the word dirty, its first and last letters, are taken

parts.note: outer letters of dirty
nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A description of a squalid, horrible home.
explanation.definitionFit: A house can mean a royal or noble family line, as in the House of Windsor, which is a dynasty.

clue.text: City left in the past, say

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
said is the past tense of say

explanation.surface: A city someone left long ago, or so they claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Said is an Egyptian city at the northern end of the Suez Canal.

clue.text: I can stop former golfer showing strain

indicators.note: I is able to plug the name, going into its middle

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros, the late Spanish golf champion

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they can halt a retired golfer who is visibly tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like stress; it is the verb for passing liquid through a mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A sieve is a mesh utensil; to sieve food is to strain it, separating liquid from solids.

clue.text: Take care of leg's connective tissue

parts.note: to tend is to look after
the leg side in cricket is also called the on side, so on is the leg's name

explanation.surface: Someone nurses an injured leg's sinew.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side; the surface makes leg a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a tough band of fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Revolutionary procedure reveals colour scheme

indicators.note: turning over means the hidden run is read backwards, upwards in a down clue
the word procedure shows a run of letters inside it

parts.note: letters two to six of procedure, which then read backwards

explanation.surface: A radical new method uncovers a decorating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the style of a room's furnishing and decoration, including its colours.

clue.text: Attempt to pack new hamper

indicators.note: the attempt packs the letter inside itself

parts.note: a bid is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fill a fresh picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' poses as a basket at the end of the picnic scene; it is the verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind is to tie up or restrict, so it means to hamper or hinder movement.

clue.text: Polish lecturer in view

indicators.note: the lecturer goes inside the view

parts.note: to gaze is to view steadily; a gaze is a view

explanation.surface: A Polish academic is in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start pretends to be the nationality; it is the verb for making shiny.
explanation.definitionFit: To glaze is to give a smooth glossy coat, which is a way of polishing a surface.

clue.text: Sligo surprisingly welcomes mysterious influential Russians?

indicators.note: the jumbled town takes the other word in
the letters of Sligo turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: arch means knowing and secretive, with hidden meaning

explanation.surface: An Irish town unexpectedly hosts some shadowy, powerful Russian visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: OLIGS, the anagram of Sligo, goes around ARCH. Sligo is a town in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchs are the super-rich businessmen who gained great power in Russia after the Soviet era; the question mark shows they need not be Russian.

clue.text: Parliamentarian fighters were fighting with my old man

indicators.note: the words are in a scrap, thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's father fought on the Roundhead side in the English Civil War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old man' is British slang for one's father (or husband).
explanation.definitionFit: The New Model Army was the professional force raised by Parliament in 1645 to fight the Royalists in the English Civil War.
